This harness demonstrates the first local owned .cjs source UI flow, rather than completion of the entire original issue #15. It does not reduce the ten original requiredFutureEvidence requirements.
Use only synthetic Codex CLIs and synthetic model metadata; do not use external AI, accounts, SSH, real user projects, or user profiles.
UI configuration save and start/stop/restart use actual renderer behavior. Agents use actual agent.start/read/cancel and actual CLI exit. Do not inject DB agent states.
Service evidence compares a private loopback native button → actual HTTP POST → actual async file save → GET/DOM/PID/instance. A ready 200 response alone does not establish success.
The execution SHA is a prelaunch file snapshot. Linking it to a known synthetic server's self-report does not establish general loaded-byte attestation or URL ownership.
Preserve original app-host and native-source screenshots separately. Do not describe the host's white native area or DOM remaining after server exit as a service error screen.
Actual Electron beforeunload/close/closed/quit events run, while the OS-native confirmation/error dialog choices and presentation use the stated fixtures.

A failed global quit may already have drained some other owned services. Assess B preservation only at the selected A restart checkpoint, and separately record B's state and manual UI restart after a blocked global quit.
PID reuse, forced crash, SSH, host reboot, native checks on other OSes or installed apps, and the entire existing common QA suite remain separately unexecuted.

On failure, attempt only exact owned IPC stop, actual agent cancellation, and release of own fixture latches. Do not send signals, use killall or forced app.exit, or adopt external PIDs. Apps with unconfirmed cleanup may remain for root observation and must not be reported as successful.
